title: Detecting Argument-Swap Bugs Using Context-Enhanced Code Representations
abstract: arXiv:2609.17844v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Names of source code elements convey rich semantic information and have been widely used in software engineering tasks such as bug detection, code completion, type prediction, and code classification. Prior studies exploit lexical similarity between method arguments and formal parameter names to detect bugs caused by incorrectly ordered arguments, typically relying on establishing mappings between method calls and their corresponding definitions. However, such mappings are often difficult to obtain in dynamically typed languages like Python. In this paper, we present BugProbe, a learning-based approach for detecting incorrectly ordered arguments in Python method calls that does not require call-to-definition mappings. translated_title: 使用上下文增强的代码表示检测参数交换错误
translated_abstract: 源代码元素的名称蕴含着丰富的语义信息，已被广泛应用于错误检测、代码补全、类型预测和代码分类等软件工程任务中。先前的研究利用方法实参与形式参数名之间的词汇相似性来检测由实参顺序错误引起的缺陷，这通常依赖于建立方法调用与其对应定义之间的映射关系。然而，在Python等动态类型语言中，这种映射关系往往难以获得。在本文中，我们提出了BugProbe，一种基于学习的方法，用于检测Python方法调用中的实参顺序错误，且无需调用到定义的映射。我们的方法利用多种上下文信息来源，包括局部上下文和实参使用上下文，并将基于名称的相似性与机器学习相结合，构建具有强表达能力的方法调用表示。
tldr: 提出了BugProbe，一种无需调用-定义映射、通过融合局部上下文与实参使用上下文并结合名称相似性与机器学习来构建代码表示，从而检测Python方法调用中实参顺序错误的基于学习的方法。
en_tdlr: BugProbe, a learning-based approach that detects argument-swap bugs in Python method calls without requiring call-to-definition mappings, by leveraging contextual information (local context and argument usage context) combined with name-based similarity and machine learning to build expressive method call representations.
